rationale: Both split the sorted counts into layers and then trade each 5+3 pair for two groups of four, which is the correct and well-known approach. A adds a second trade that turns a 3-group plus a 1-group into a 4-group, and that trade is wrong. The single-book layer is always a copy of the most-stocked title, which is already in the 3-group, so the four books are not distinct. For example, the basket [1,1,2,3] has only three titles, but A charges 2560 for it instead of 2960. A's comment also misstates the 3+1 cost as 3680 when it is 2160+800 = 2960. B has only the valid trade and explains clearly why it keeps every title's count unchanged. It also builds the group counts and the total with loops instead of hand-written terms. B is correct beyond the tests and clearer; A has a real bug in its logic and a misleading comment.
